candidate.educational_objective: Apply the cited evidence to recognize the uniquely safest or most accurate nursing response in the clinical situation tested by V2-Q0139.

options.A: The value is considered optimal in young adulthood, so risk assessment and lifestyle counseling can be deferred until the client reaches age 40.
options.B: The result automatically establishes familial hypercholesterolemia and requires the same treatment pathway as every adult with LDL-C at least 190 mg/dL in all cases.
options.C: The value should be ignored if triglycerides are normal because the 2026 guideline no longer uses LDL-C in primary-prevention treatment decisions.
options.D: LDL-C at least 160 mg/dL in young adulthood supports earlier risk discussion and consideration of lipid-lowering therapy rather than relying on one universal target.

candidate.rationale: The 2026 ACC/AHA dyslipidemia guideline emphasizes earlier prevention and specifically identifies LDL-C ≥160 mg/dL in young adulthood as a setting in which pharmacotherapy may be considered, alongside lifestyle optimization and individualized risk assessment. It does not equate 165 mg/dL with the ≥190 mg/dL severe-hypercholesterolemia pathway in every patient.
candidate.source_claim_supported: 2026 guideline supports early consideration of pharmacotherapy in young adults with LDL-C ≥160 mg/dL and uses individualized risk assessment rather than a single universal rule.
